sample_unit: documents (verbal autopsies and pediatric/maternal clinical abstractions)

links.outcome: De-identification F1-score for PII entities across document types
links.effect: Dates and locations F1 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.93) to 0.98 (0.97-0.98); names F1 0.75 (0.70-0.80) for VAs to 0.94 (0.91-0.96) for MCAs; IAA kappa=0.98.
links.quote: The final system demonstrated consistency across document types for dates and locations, achieving F1-scores between 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.93) and 0.98 (95% CI 0.97-0.98).

unlisted_practices: Multi-agent LLM reviewer agent as post-processing check for residual PII in de-identification
Hybrid ensemble of LLM, off-the-shelf tool, and rule-based module for de-identification of non-Global-North clinical text

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks a multi-agent LLM-based de-identification framework for clinical narratives from LMICs against human annotations, without comparing organizational deployment practices or safeguards.
